aspects.says: The comparison at each boundary of a range decides which branch the boundary value takes.
basis: section:An else-if Chain Runs the First Branch That Holds, So the Order Is the Specification

aspects.says: An else-if chain runs only the first branch whose condition holds, so a special case inside a range must come before the range.
basis: section:An else-if Chain Runs the First Branch That Holds, So the Order Is the Specification

aspects.says: An if with a constant false condition compiles and its body is not generated, while a while loop with one is an unreachable statement.
basis: section:The Compiler Judges an if by Its Constants and Its Exits, Never by What Its Conditions Mean

aspects.says: javac's definite-assignment rules don't evaluate non-constant conditions, so an else-if chain without a final else leaves a final local possibly unassigned.
basis: section:The Compiler Judges an if by Its Constants and Its Exits, Never by What Its Conditions Mean

aspects.says: An else belongs to the nearest if that has none, whatever the indentation says; braces decide the binding.
basis: section:An else Belongs to the Nearest if, Whatever the Indentation Says

aspects.says: A pattern variable from a negated instanceof is in scope after the if only when the if's body cannot complete normally.
basis: section:The Compiler Judges an if by Its Constants and Its Exits, Never by What Its Conditions Mean

aspects.says: A conditional expression with an int and a double operand has type double, so an int result comes out as a Double.
basis: section:A Conditional Expression Takes Its Type From Both Branches, So a Primitive on One Side Unboxes the Other

aspects.says: A conditional expression with an int on one side and an Integer on the other has type int, so a null Integer throws NullPointerException where if/else would return null.
basis: section:A Conditional Expression Takes Its Type From Both Branches, So a Primitive on One Side Unboxes the Other
